## macOS (arm64) variant: continuous `.dylib` leak during a session, ~1.6 GB/hour

Same root mechanism as this report (bunfs embedded-library extraction into the temp dir with no cleanup), but on macOS the artifact extension is `.dylib` and the leak is **continuous while a session runs**, not just once per launch. Worth fixing here since it fills internal SSDs on Macs quickly.

### Environment
- opencode `1.18.23`, macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83), arm64
- Bundled Bun runtime `v24.18.0`

### Observed behavior
- Files matching `$TMPDIR`/`.5bff*-00000000.dylib` (also saw `.5bfe*`, `.b9de*`, `.b9df*` prefixes over time) — Mach-O 64-bit dynamically linked shared library, arm64, ~3.6 MB each.
- Leak is **continuous during active usage**, not one file per launch: measured 9,316 files / 33 GB accumulated in ~21 hours ≈ **1.6 GB/hour** (~one file every 8 s), with `lsof` showing the running `opencode` process holding them open.
- On a 256 GB-class internal SSD this drove the disk to ~50% full within a day; a prior occurrence reached ~71 GB before manual cleanup.

### Reproduction
1. Run opencode TUI, keep an active session going for a few hours.
2. `find "$TMPDIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '.5bff*-*.dylib' | wc -l` → grows hundreds of files/hour.
3. `lsof +D "$TMPDIR"` → owned by the `opencode` process.

### Expected behavior
Extracted runtime libraries are either reused across launches / stable-named or removed when no longer needed. The temp dir should not grow unboundedly during a single session.

### Workaround (safe on macOS)
Deleting an open file on macOS is safe — space is reclaimed when the holding process exits and Bun re-JITs on demand:
```
find "$TMPDIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '.*-*.dylib' -delete
```
I installed a 30-minute purge agent to contain this; that is mitigation, not a fix.

### Notes
- This is the macOS sibling of the Linux `.so` leaks (#42700, #16996): same bunfs `$bunfs/root/lib…` extraction pattern, extension differs by platform.
- No plugins or config involved; reproduces with default setup.

Noting here for completeness: this same bunfs temp-artifact leak is still active and has a macOS sibling. On macOS (arm64) opencode leaks ~3.6 MB `.dylib` files (`$TMPDIR`/`.5bff*-00000000.dylib`, etc.) **continuously during a session** — measured ~1.6 GB/hour (33 GB in 21 h on opencode 1.18.23). Tracked in the open issue #42700, which remains unfixed. Workaround: `find "$TMPDIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '.*-*.dylib' -delete` (safe on macOS; space frees when the process exits).

Title gen doesn't fire on /goal's first prompt: the trigger runs (inbox promotion → SessionRunner title fiber), but SessionTitle.generate reads its input from SessionHistory.firstUserMessage, which filters on type = 'user' — and synthetic inbox items persist as type: 'synthetic'. So the title silently no-ops (if (!firstUser) return) until a real user message exists in the session. Fix is probably falling back to a synthetic message for title input when no user message exists yet.

This appears related to #45204 and #38333, but there is an important additional detail in my case.

The requested model openrouter/xiaomi/mimo-v2.5 is actually present in the WSL sidecar /provider catalog and works correctly through the CLI:

opencode run -m openrouter/xiaomi/mimo-v2.5 "OK"

However, Desktop's visibility filtering hides the OpenRouter model because there is no persisted model.v1.user visibility override for it.

At the same time, Desktop has a visible/recent model:

opencode/mimo-v2.5-free

The fallback then silently changes the complete model identity from:

providerID=openrouter
modelID=xiaomi/mimo-v2.5

to:

providerID=opencode
modelID=mimo-v2.5-free

The request is subsequently sent to OpenCode Zen instead of OpenRouter and fails with:

Forbidden: {"model":"mimo-v2.5-free"}

So this is not simply an unavailable model being replaced by another model. The fallback changes the provider as well, without informing the user.

I was able to confirm that the OpenRouter model exists in the provider catalog and that the OpenRouter credentials and model itself are functional.

This may be useful as an additional reproduction case for #45204/#38333, particularly around provider identity preservation during model fallback.

Too opaque for my blood. So long, and thank you for goFish. No serious product manages its transparency this way. I am very disappointed to report our latest findings to the committee. We cannot revoke our good faith investments. For those who are curious, that one query cost me an addition $1.53, which is more than entire platform developments cost me in previous weeks. We have shipped entire repositories for that cost. The answer, for those who are curious, is presumably because we switched to Qwen 3.6 Plus (c.f. Apple) after the Ox Alpha Free (x-preview-f-free) errors, and the entire 762K context had to be sent fresh without cache on the new model. However, I do not even see that in its analysis, which is so perfectly pointed for these experiences. I am very sorry and we do not wish to explore these experiences any further with any of the formerly named providers. Hit the gym, hit the showers, have a beer if such is your fashionable tastes and enjoy yourself a very merry rest of nights. We are going to have a laugh. We must hold true to our present and international standing and shall only refuse to revoke our good faith investments.

Is this actually confirmed as a real issue and/or fixed? In v2 specifically.

I'm really having trouble understanding the issue tracking around this. In particular, issues like this that describe a clear catastrophic failure of compaction appear to be getting closed by a bot as "not planned".

Either it is confirmed and compaction is entirely broken in all conceivable ways, or it's not reproduced and not a real issue and something else is happening. Not planned auto-closing doesn't make sense here.

I'm seeing behavior where, after compaction, the agent appears to have completely forgotten its own definition. It looks as though the agent definition that was present during initialization is not included in the post-compaction context.

If that is actually happening, this isn't a minor context-loss bug. It means the agent can lose the instructions that define what the agent is, what it is supposed to do, and how it is supposed to behave. That would make the compaction mechanism fundamentally incorrect.

The expected semantics of compaction seem unambiguous:

Initial agent context + session history → compaction → initial agent context + compacted representation of the session

The agent's definition is initialization context, not disposable conversation history. It therefore needs to remain present after compaction. Otherwise the resulting context is not equivalent to a compacted continuation of the original session; it is a differently initialized agent with a summary of the previous conversation.

So... is this issue real or not? If it's real how is it any other work is done on anything other than fixing what amounts to entirely functionally incorrect and broken?

Some clarification on the actual status of this from the developers would be much appreciated. A closed as "not a bug" would make much more sense here if it's not a bug. Or if it is a bug, I think anyone would agree it's a p0 and open.

I guess in general I'd really appreciate if opencode could improve its process / issue tracking. Every time I have issues I seem to find something related that got closed as not planned like this. Makes it really hard to know what is an open issue that needs a workaround if there's no real tracking just auto closed stuff into a general bucket of "not planned".

I understand it's an open source volunteer project and kudos on all the amazing work, but the issue tracking being better would really be nice so the users can eagerly await the fixes knowing it is a bug or not, and find some workaround in the meantime. It's all guessing now and having your ai dig through the source to try and figure out the real state of things.

This is a small, isolated fix (+87/−3, 2 files): `SessionRunnerModel.fromCatalogModel` currently routes only `@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, and `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`+url, so every `openrouter` (`@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider`) and `groq` (`@ai-sdk/groq`) model lists but silently fails to dispatch with `UnsupportedApiError` the moment a session drains. The fix consults the existing `openai-compatible-profile.ts` table (which already classifies both) after the three package checks — no new dependency, and providers outside that table are unaffected.

Verified live against a branch build with real groq + OpenRouter keys in an isolated `XDG_*` home: all three test models answered `ok`/`stop`; `supported()` and dispatch share the same helper so selection and dispatch cannot disagree. Happy to rebase or split further if that helps review.

> I reproduced this and isolated the failing path further.
> 
> Environment:
> 
> * Windows 11
> * OpenCode Go
> * Model: `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`
> * OpenCodex 2.32.0
> * Codex Desktop
> * Same OpenCode Go API key for all tests
> 
> Results:
> 
> 1. Muse works normally inside the OpenCode app.
> 2. Direct request to the Responses API works:
> 
> `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses`
> 
> with:
> 
> `model: muse-spark-1.2-contributor`
> 
> Result:
> 
> `HTTP 200` `status: completed`
> 
> So the model, account, API key and OpenCode Go access are all working.
> 
> 3. The same model routed through the Chat Completions protocol fails consistently:
> 
> `/v1/chat/completions`
> 
> Result:
> 
> `HTTP 500` `Internal server error`
> 
> 4. OpenCodex debug confirms the failing request is using:
> 
> `adapter: openai-chat` `model: muse-spark-1.2-contributor` `stream: true`
> 
> 5. After a completely fresh OpenCodex 2.32.0 reinstall, other models through the same setup work correctly:
> 
> * GPT-5.6 Luna: 200
> * DeepSeek V4 Flash: 200
> * Gemini 3.7 Flash: 200
> * Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor: 500
> 
> This therefore appears isolated to Muse + the Chat Completions API path.
> 
> The OpenCode Go documentation currently lists Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor under `/v1/responses`, and our direct test confirms that endpoint works.
> 
> Possible fixes:
> 
> * Make `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` work correctly through `/v1/chat/completions`, or
> * Return a clear 4xx unsupported-protocol error instead of HTTP 500 when Muse is called through Chat Completions, and
> * Ensure clients can reliably discover that this model requires the Responses API.
> 
> This also seems related to the existing Muse Chat Completions streaming/schema issues, but in this case the request fails immediately with HTTP 500 before a usable response is returned.
